summary: NDR feed s155_double is degraded: 19.0% one-way TCP sessions (92/485) breaks bidirectional analysis and 20.24 Gbps microburst exceeds 10 Gbps NDR port (202% capacity) causing drops.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction for ~19% of TCP sessions. Both directions likely arrive on separate TAP/SPAN inputs but are not aggregated to the same tool port, or asymmetric routing is tapped on only one side, so the NDR sees half-sessions.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions to reassemble TCP, track state, and detect C2/lateral movement. One-way flows cause missed detections, broken session reconstruction, and false positives for scan/anomaly models.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate complementary directions at the packet broker and hash both sides of a flow to the same NDR port to restore complete bidirectional visibility required by NDR.

findings.root_cause: 1 ms microburst peaked at 20.24 Gbps on a 10 Gbps NDR port (202% of capacity). Aggregated feed bursts exceed single tool port line rate, causing buffer overrun and drops before the NDR can process.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR with full-payload requirement will drop packets under overload, creating blind spots, missed IDS signatures, and incomplete flow records during peak bursts.

recommended_fix.why: Load-balance the feed across 2-3x 10G NDR ports (or upgrade to 25/40G) with bidirectional hash to absorb 20+ Gbps bursts without drops while preserving full payload; add selective filtering only if extra ports unavailable.
